issues.legal_issue: A bail order may be set aside on appeal when the court granting bail fails to assess material evidence and the gravity of the alleged offence.
material_facts: The accused faced allegations of participating in a serious violent incident involving a death and injuries, and the prosecution alleged that he was the kingpin of a criminal conspiracy.
The Court reviewed a recording that prima facie showed a group committing the offence with deadly weapons and sticks.

The High Court granted bail principally because no injury was attributed personally to the accused and the trial would take considerable time, without adequately assessing the material and the need for custodial interrogation.
issues.conclusion: The grant of bail was set aside and the authorities were directed to take the accused into custody.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, bail must be considered with prudent legal perception of the record, including the prima facie case, gravity of the offence, and relevant circumstances; the Court found those matters were not properly appreciated here.

rule.if: appeal_challenging_bail_grant and serious_violent_allegations and supporting_material_indicates_prima_facie_involvement and (bail_court_failed_to_assess_material or custodial_interrogation_needed)

predicates.appeal_challenging_bail_grant: The proceeding is an appeal challenging an order granting bail.
predicates.serious_violent_allegations: The accused is alleged to have been involved in a serious violent offence.
predicates.supporting_material_indicates_prima_faci: Material before the court indicates a prima facie connection between the accused and the alleged offence.
predicates.bail_court_failed_to_assess_material: The court granting bail did not adequately assess material facts relevant to the bail decision.
predicates.custodial_interrogation_needed: The circumstances indicate that custodial interrogation of the accused is needed.
predicates.bail_grant_set_aside: The bail order is set aside.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges bail granted despite serious violent allegations and material indicating prima facie involvement, the grant is set aside if the bail court failed to assess relevant material or custodial interrogation is needed.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge to the legality of an order granting bail for non-consideration of material does not require proof of a later breach of bail conditions.
material_facts: The appellant challenged the original order granting bail on the ground that material available on the record had not been considered.
No supervening event involving breach of bail conditions was pleaded.
The respondent argued that bail could not be cancelled without a breach of its conditions.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the challenge concerned the legal sustainability of the original bail order, not cancellation for breach, and could proceed without proof of a breach of bail conditions.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished a legal challenge to an order granting bail for non-consideration of material from cancellation of bail following a supervening event or breach of conditions, relying on State through C.B.I. v. Amarmani Tripathi, (2005) 8 SCC 21, and Prakash Kadam v. Ramprasad Vishwanath Gupta, (2011) 6 SCC 189.

predicates.appeal_challenging_initial_bail_grant: The proceeding challenges the original decision granting bail rather than seeking cancellation solely for later conduct.
predicates.challenge_based_on_nonconsideration_of_m: The challenger alleges that the bail court failed to consider material available when it made the grant.
predicates.challenge_permitted_without_proof_of_bai: The legality of the original bail grant may be reviewed without proof of a later breach of bail conditions.

issues.definition: An appeal challenging an initial bail grant for failure to consider available material may proceed even if no later breach of bail conditions is alleged.

issues.legal_issue: A foreign national is not entitled to special consideration in the application of bail law on the basis of nationality.
material_facts: The accused was a British national.
The Court found a prima facie case that he had engaged in the alleged criminal activity with others.
The Court considered the accused's nationality while reviewing the bail order.
issues.conclusion: The Court refused special consideration based on foreign nationality and held that the law applies equally to accused persons irrespective of nationality.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and stated that every accused is the same in the eyes of the law irrespective of nationality.

predicates.bail_proceeding: The proceeding concerns whether an accused should receive bail.
predicates.accused_is_foreign_national: The accused is a national of a country other than the country where the proceeding is brought.
predicates.nationality_does_not_warrant_special_bai: Foreign nationality alone does not justify special consideration in deciding bail.

issues.definition: In a bail proceeding, an accused's foreign nationality alone does not justify special treatment.

issues.legal_issue: Bail granted solely on parity with another accused cannot stand when the bail order providing the basis for parity is set aside.
material_facts: The High Court granted bail to the accused on the basis of parity with another accused.
The Court set aside the other accused's bail order in the companion appeal.
The Court also considered the circumstances of the accused's case and found it unsuitable for bail for the reasons already given.
issues.conclusion: The Court set aside the bail order that had been granted on parity.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that setting aside the bail order relied on for parity removed the footing for the later grant; it also found the case unsuitable for bail on the reasons stated in the companion appeal.

predicates.appeal_challenging_bail_grant: The proceeding is an appeal challenging an order granting bail.
predicates.bail_based_on_parity: The bail court granted bail by relying on parity with another accused.
predicates.parity_bail_order_set_aside: The bail order used as the basis for parity has been set aside.
predicates.parity_based_bail_grant_set_aside: The bail grant based on parity is set aside.

issues.definition: When an appealed bail grant rests on parity with an order that has been set aside, the parity-based grant is set aside.

issues.legal_issue: A superior court must not direct a subordinate court to grant bail mandatorily, and a bail order obtained through such a process may be set aside.
material_facts: In an anticipatory-bail proceeding, the High Court ordered that the accused be admitted to bail if he surrendered before the trial court within a specified time.
The trial court then released the accused on bail in compliance with the High Court's direction.
The High Court later dismissed the anticipatory-bail application as infructuous after the accused had obtained bail.
The accused had been declared a proclaimed offender before the bail grant, but that fact was not considered by the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the High Court's mandatory direction breached the independence of the subordinate court and that the circuitous process was a gross abuse of court process undertaken in bad faith; it set aside the bail order and directed that the accused be taken into custody.
issues.legal_principle: Relying on Madan Mohan v. State of Rajasthan, Criminal Appeal No. 2178 of 2017, the Court held that courts cannot issue mandatory directions that breach the independence of subordinate courts. It also treated the circuitous method of obtaining bail as an abuse of process and noted that the accused's proclaimed-offender status had been overlooked.

rule.if: appeal_challenging_bail_grant and anticipatory_bail_proceeding and superior_court_mandated_subordinate_bail and bail_obtained_through_circuitous_process and proclaimed_offender_status_ignored

predicates.appeal_challenging_bail_grant: The proceeding is an appeal challenging an order granting bail.
predicates.anticipatory_bail_proceeding: The underlying proceeding sought protection from arrest before the accused was taken into custody.
predicates.superior_court_mandated_subordinate_bail: A superior court directed a subordinate court to admit the accused to bail rather than leaving the bail decision to that court.
predicates.bail_obtained_through_circuitous_process: The accused obtained bail through a sequence in which compliance with the superior court's direction led to bail and the underlying application was then dismissed as infructuous.
predicates.proclaimed_offender_status_ignored: The accused had been declared a proclaimed offender before bail was granted, and that status was not considered.
predicates.bail_grant_set_aside: The bail order is set aside.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges bail obtained in an anticipatory-bail proceeding through a mandatory direction to a subordinate court and a circuitous process that overlooks proclaimed-offender status, the bail grant is set aside.
